concept: How does the water cycle move water around the Earth?
title: Sky River Loop
tagline: Water vanishes into air, then falls again

science.hiddenLaw: In a closed Earth system total water mass is conserved while solar thermal energy drives evaporation (liquid → invisible water vapor) at a rate that increases with available energy/temperature, and cooling of moist air below its saturation (dew-point) temperature drives condensation to liquid droplets/ice and precipitation (vapor → liquid/solid), cycling water through ocean/land ↔ atmosphere reservoirs.
science.plainStatement: The Sun's heat turns liquid water into invisible vapor that rises; when that moist air cools high up it condenses into cloud droplets and falls as rain or snow. The same water just cycles around — never destroyed or created — powered by heating below and cooling above.
misconceptions: Water disappears when it evaporates and is newly created when it rains — mass is not conserved.
Evaporation only happens at boiling (100°C); water cannot become vapor at room temperature.
Clouds are made of water vapor gas and rain falls because clouds get too heavy, get squeezed, or are blown together — not because vapor cools and condenses.
The water cycle has a start/end or is driven by wind, not by the Sun's energy input and subsequent cooling aloft.

story.mystery: Where does vanished water go, and why does rain return?
story.goal: Tune sun and temperatures to trace the hidden loop.

predictions.prompt: What happens to total water after 1000 steps with strong sun and cold high air?
options: Water is lost when it evaporates
New water is created when it rains

predictions.prompt: Can water become invisible vapor at 20°C without boiling?
options: Yes, sun warmth lifts it slowly

predictions.prompt: Why does rain fall from clouds?
options: Moist air cooled and condensed into droplets
Clouds are vapor gas that got too heavy
Clouds were squeezed together by wind

predictions.prompt: What powers the whole water loop?
options: Sun heating below and cooling above
Cycle has a start and end point

transfer.setup: A sealed glass dome in a desert holds 1000 units of water with bright lamps heating the ground to 30°C and a freezer roof at -10°C.
transfer.question: After many days sealed, what will the water do?
options: All become cloud, no rain falls

checks.description: Control: with no solar energy input evaporation stops — remove cause, effect disappears
With solar energy, evaporation rate becomes positive and vapor accumulates
Control: with warm air aloft (no cooling below dew point) precipitation stays near zero even with vapor present
Cooling moist air below saturation drives condensation and precipitation
Total water mass (ocean + vapor + cloud + land) stays constant — evaporation does not destroy water
